verdict.reasoning: Patient reports dizziness with room spinning and unsteadiness for about 2 hours: “Started probably about two hours ago… the room is sort of spinning… I can't walk properly… I don't feel like I'm stable… it's there, the whole time… So it's there now for the past two hours you'd say, yeah? Patient: Yep.”

Onset while making breakfast and persisting: “I was just actually making my husband some breakfast… I just suddenly felt very fuzzy and dizzy… And is it there now, continuously now? Patient: Yeah it's, it's there, the whole time… So it's there now for the past two hours you'd say, yeah? Patient: Yep.”

Ear buzzing and nausea without vomiting are described: “my ears are buzzing a bit… they're feeling a bit off… It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears” and “Have you been physically sick? Patient: No, but now I'm feeling very sick. Doctor: Nausea, OK.”

Prior similar brief episode a month ago: “I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago… it settled quite quickly” and when asked “how long did that episode last for?” patient replies “Probably only about five, ten minutes.”

Patient denies these associated features: ear pain/discharge (“Any kind of ear pain or ear discharge? Patient: No, nothing.”), hearing problems (“do you have any problems hearing at the moment?… Patient: No… I can hear everything.”), recent viral illness/URTI (“Did you have any kind of viral illness…? Patient: No… No cold, cough, nothing.”), temperature (“Do you have a temperature at all? Patient: I don't think so”), and limb weakness (“So there's no weakness of your arms and legs. Patient: No.”).
Past medical history given: “is there any medical conditions you'd like to tell me?… Patient: Um, I've had premature ovarian failure…”
HRT use is stated: “I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT.”
No allergies reported: “OK, do you have any allergies at all? Patient: No.”

Doctor diagnoses likely labyrinthitis with vertigo and acknowledges nausea and ear buzzing (tinnitus-like): “the most common… diagnosis… is something called labyrinthitis… so that you won't feel as if you're going around in a boat” and earlier “ear's buzzing” plus “Nausea, OK.”

Prescription details: “I'll send the a prescription… looks like it's the Lloyd pharmacy on our system. Is that correct? Patient: Yeah… it's called , yeah? It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about ten days worth.”

Plan for in-person review with otoscopy, BP, and gait/neuro check: “I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears… while you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how your walking and everything is.”

Safety net for ED/A&E: “if you double up any weakness of your legs or arms or, or, you know, a sudden headache… or you start being violently sick with it, then you know, you would need to take your to A and E.” This corresponds to advice for limb weakness, severe headache, or intractable vomiting.
Instruction to call support to book appointment: “Just make sure you call support to book that appointment, OK? Patient: I will, thank you very much.”
